{{Short description|Swedish mathematician (born 1953)}}
'''Nils Jonas Dencker''' (born 14 December 1953 in [[Lund]]) is a Swedish mathematician. Dencker earned his doctorate from [[Lund University]] in 1981 under supervision of [[Lars Hörmander]], and is a professor of mathematics at Lund University.  From 1981 until 1983, he was the [[C. L. E. Moore instructor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="CV">{{cite web |title=CURRICULUM VITAE |url=http://www.maths.lth.se/matematiklu/personal/dencker/CV20.pdf |website=Lund University |access-date=30 April 2021}}</ref> 

He won the 2005 [[Clay Research Award]] for his proof of the [[Nirenberg–Treves conjecture]].<ref>{{citation|last=Dencker|first=Nils |title=The resolution of the Nirenberg–Treves Conjecture |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=163 |issue=2 |year=2006|pages=405–444 |doi=10.4007/annals.2006.163.405 |arxiv=math/0303201 |s2cid=16630732 }}</ref>

Dencker has been a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] since 2008. He was an invited speaker at the [[European Congress of Mathematics]] in Amsterdam in 2008, and at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Hyderabad]], India, in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.icm2010.in/scientific-program/invited-speakers|title=Invited speakers at ICM2012}}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>
